---
title: "phit-polyfill"
---

phit-polyfill is a pure-PHP implementation of the
[phit](https://github.com/phpstats/phit) native extension. It defines phit's
functions in the `Phit` namespace when the extension is not loaded. Names,
parameter names, defaults, result keys, warnings, and exception codes are the
same as the extension's. Code written against phit therefore runs unchanged on
hosts where the extension cannot be installed, such as shared hosting or a
managed platform without custom extensions. When the extension is loaded, the
polyfill defines nothing and phit is used.

The implementations are ports of phit's Rust code. On every input in the test
suites, the polyfill returns the same bits as the extension.

## Installation

```bash
composer require phpstats/phit-polyfill
```

PHP 8.3 or later is required. Composer loads the polyfill's `bootstrap.php`
automatically. For each function the polyfill implements, the bootstrap
declares it in the `Phit` namespace only if `function_exists()` reports that it
is missing and the `phit` extension is not loaded.

## Usage

Import functions with `use function`, or call them by their qualified names.

```php
use function Phit\fit_ols;

$fit = fit_ols(
    x: [[1.2, 0.4], [2.3, 1.1], [3.1, 0.9], [4.8, 2.2], [5.0, 1.7]],
    y: [2.1, 4.2, 5.8, 8.1, 10.2],
);

$fit['coefficients'];  // intercept first, as with the extension
$fit['p_values'];
```

The same code runs with the extension. Install phit where you can, because it
is faster, and keep the polyfill as a Composer dependency for the hosts where
you cannot.

## Checking what is available

`Phit\Polyfill\Polyfill` reports which functions the polyfill implements and
whether the extension is loaded.

```php
use Phit\Polyfill\Polyfill;

Polyfill::supports('Phit\fit_logistic');  // true
Polyfill::supports('Phit\read_csv');      // false: needs the extension
Polyfill::nativeLoaded();                 // whether phit is loaded
```

`Polyfill::implementation('Phit\fit_ols')` returns the polyfill's callable
even when the extension is loaded. The parity tests and the benchmarks use it
to run both implementations in one process.

## Versions

Each polyfill release reproduces one phit commit, pinned in
`tests/fixtures/REFERENCE`. Version 0.1.0 reproduces phit
[`1bf73bd`](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/commit/1bf73bd3bdf66f825039713ac58157d0f9d6ddf9).
Neither package has a tagged release yet.
